newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB raises net profit forecast for UBS.
newsitem.headline: CSFB raises net profit forecast for UBS.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston raised its 1997 and 1998 net profit estimates for Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) after the bank disclosed first-ever detailed divisional results.
But analyst Madeleine Hofmann maintained her recommendation of "hold" for UBS shares. UBS holds its annual shareholding meeting on Thursday.

Hofmann said UBS, presenting its divisional results to financial analysts last week, had also revealed that ordinary provisions for lower-risk loans were lower than expected at about 300 million Swiss francs in 1996.
"Based on lower estimates for provisions, we have raised our net profit estimates for 1997 and 1998 by seven percent and four percent, respectively," Hofmann wrote in a study.

Hofmann told Reuters the reference to provisions meant ordinary provisions for lower-risk credits, as opposed to an extraordinary charge of three billion Swiss francs UBS took last year to cover higher risk loans in economiclaly stagnant Switzerland.
The new estimates for net profit were 2,502 million Swiss francs in 1997 and 2,698 in 1998 after an extraordinary loss of 350 million last year and 1995 net of 1,673 million.
Hofmann raised her earnings per share (EPS) estimates for 1997 to 97.5 Swiss francs from 90.0 and for 1998 to 105.2 francs from 101.2. EPS last year was minus 13.6 Swiss francs after 65.6 in 1995.

She said UBS remained a "hold" because of uncertain prospects for financial markets and because evidence was lacking that UBS had achieved sustainable growth in profitability in its difficult Swiss domestic business.

Hofmann said the information on last year's ordinary provisions came from a UBS meting for financial analysts on April 7 to unveil the bank's first-ever brekadon of annual results by its main business divisions Swiss retail, corporate and institutional finnace, and trading and sales.
"The provisions were discussed...and ordinary provisions for good quality risk were only about 300 million (Swiss francs), less than expected," she told Reuters.
